part.text: {"variants":[{"id":"V1","title":"Drift probes against Kimina's statement judge, with a public audit set","text":"Probe Kimina-Autoformalizer-7B's activations while it writes definitions and statements, to flag when it has quietly strengthened a hypothesis or guessed a convention, in service of the semantic-correctness gate inside the Kimina expert-iteration loop. Because no programme publishes an expert-labelled real-misformalization test set, build and release one independently: faithful/drifted pairs audited by mathematicians, held out from synthetic-drift training. Then score a frozen-model linear probe head-to-head against the judges these loops actually run — Kimina's judge prompt and the Qwen2.5-72B and QwQ-32B judges in the Kimina and Goedel-Prover pipelines — not against text-only baselines. The chain is otherwise unchanged: expert-labelled pairs, one forward pass per statement, a probe fit, held-out evaluation, with synthetic drift generated in parallel by counterfactual perturbation.","root_link":"B4 / framer 4.3: whether a readable drift trace inside the generator can shrink the human audit set — here measured directly against the gate that decides which candidate Lean statements enter Kimina-Prover's RL problem set.","compute_open":"Quantity is statements times judges and models scored: statements cached for probing plus the same statements pushed through the production judge ensemble. The most reported remains 950 SMT-LIB encodings and one 27B verifier; unknown above that is whether a probe beats Kimina's judge at equal audit cost and whether the released set is reusable across programmes.","sequential":"Expert audit, then one forward pass per statement to cache activations, then probe fit, then held-out evaluation, then the judge head-to-head; only the audit is serial, and synthetic perturbation plus GPU-sharded forward passes run in parallel.","changes":"Changes the comparison it is judged against (production judge ensembles rather than text-only baselines) and the programme aimed at (Kimina/Numina), while also creating the independent expert-labelled real-error set the programme check found no programme publishes. Answers gaps 1 and 5."},{"id":"V2","title":"Frozen linear probes versus a FormalAlign-style evaluator, with cross-model transfer","text":"Probe frozen Lean autoformalizers' activations while they write definitions and statements, to flag quiet hypothesis-strengthening or convention-guessing, but change the system studied to the evaluator side: run frozen-model linear probes alongside a FormalAlign-style method, a separately fine-tuned 7B evaluator trained with a contrastive loss over synthetic misalignments, on the same statements. Ask whether probe directions copied across open formalizers (7B/8B/32B) still read drift, since the card's cross-model probe-transfer arm is untested by any programme and FormalAlign is hidden-state-based but not a frozen-model probe. Keep the rest: expert-labelled faithful/unfaithful pairs, one forward pass per statement, probe fit, held-out evaluation, and synthetic-drift training generated in parallel by counterfactual perturbation. The programme payoff is the semantic-correctness gates in the Kimina and Goedel-Prover expert-iteration loops, which currently rely on ad-hoc safeguards and external judges rather than representation-level checks.","root_link":"B4 / framer 4.3: whether a misformalization the kernel cannot see leaves a readable trace inside the generator, asked here comparatively — frozen linear probe versus a fine-tuned hidden-state evaluator, and across model sizes.","compute_open":"Quantity is models and labelled statements analysed: forward passes cached per model for the probe, plus fine-tuning runs for the FormalAlign-style comparator. The most reported is nine models up to 72B on 100 training and 200 held-out math problems plus 950 SMT-LIB encodings; unknown above that is whether frozen probe directions transfer across formalizer sizes at all.","sequential":"Expert-labelled pairs, then one forward pass per statement per model to cache activations, then probe fit and evaluator fine-tune, then held-out evaluation and cross-model transfer scoring; only labelling is serial, and forward passes over statements and models run side-by-side on separate GPUs.","changes":"Changes the system studied — frozen-model linear probes benchmarked against a FormalAlign-style fine-tuned evaluator, and tested for cross-model transfer. Answers gap 3, and by producing cross-size transfer evidence it strengthens the case for validating probes inside closed formalizers such as DeepMind's."},{"id":"V3","title":"Definition-level drift probes for AlphaProof-Nexus research problems","text":"Probe the autoformalizer's activations while it writes definitions and statements, to flag quiet hypothesis-strengthening or convention-guessing, but shift the test distribution to research-level definition formalization of the kind the 2026 AlphaProof-Nexus programme targets (OEIS and Erdős problems), where a misformalized definition means the agent proves the wrong theorem. Because DeepMind's formalizer is a closed Gemini model with no activation access, run the probe on open 7B/8B/32B Lean formalizers as a proxy and state exactly what would need internal replication before transfer to AlphaProof-Nexus. Keep the rest: expert-labelled faithful/unfaithful pairs, one forward pass per statement, probe fit, held-out evaluation, and synthetic-drift training generated in parallel by counterfactual perturbation. The test set becomes definition-heavy research statements rather than competition and conjecture problems, so the lemma-level decomposition can be extended to resolve a definition into its component conditions.","root_link":"B4 / framer 4.3: whether a misformalization of the root statement or its definitions, which the kernel cannot see, leaves a readable trace inside the generator — tested at the definition level, where a wrong convention changes what is proved rather than whether it compiles.","compute_open":"Quantity is statement-runs over definition-level research statements plus formalizer sizes; the most reported is 950 SMT-LIB encodings and nine models up to 72B on 300 math problems. Unknown above that is whether drift in research-level definitions is linearly readable at all, and how far open-formalizer probes extrapolate to a closed formalizer.","sequential":"Expert-labelled definition pairs, then one forward pass per statement to cache activations, then probe fit, then held-out evaluation on research-level statements; only the expert audit is serial, and synthetic definition perturbations and GPU-sharded forward passes run in parallel.","changes":"Changes the programme aimed at and the distribution — AlphaProof-Nexus research-level definition formalization rather than competition and conjecture statements — so the lever outcome is evidence rather than extrapolation, and it confronts the closed-model access gap directly. Answers gaps 2 and 4."}]}
